sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vikas Rana
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.588 of 2019 at Police Station-Baheri, District-Bareilly under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 14.10.2019.

The following arguments made by Shri Rajesh Kumar Verma, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
Kishor vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178589425/
1
2. The applicant never harassed the deceased nor did he demand dowry.
3. The applicant is bereaved by the death of his wife.
4. The deceased was a temperamental lady who was prone to extreme reactions even over trivial issues.

5. On the fateful day, after a minor disagreement with the members of the households over the dates of deceased to visit her parental house, she flew into a fit of rage and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
6. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

7. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii). No abnormality was detected in the hyoid bone 8.
The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
9. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
10. The prerequisite for attracting the presumption and reversing the burden of proof are not established in the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case.
11. The applicant is in jail since 01.08.2019.
The applicant is a law abiding citizen and had always cooperated with the investigations and joined the trial.

The applicant never tampered with evidence nor did he influence any witness.
12.
The report sent by the learned trial court till April, 2023 records that the prosecution witnesses proposes 17 witnesses to examine to bring home the charges against the applicant.
However, only five witnesses have been examined till date.

13. The first informant who is the brother of the deceased has repudiated the prosecution case in his testimony before the learned trial court and has been declared hostile at the instance of the prosecution.
14. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and and shows no sign of early conclusion.
The applicant cannot be faulted for the delay in the trial.
15. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant without being any evidence against the applicant.

The right of the applicant Kishor vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178589425/
2 to speedy trial has been violated.

16. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
17.
The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Kishor be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 18.9.2023 Ashish Tripathi  Kishor vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178589425/
